summary: This change is limited to the release pipeline in .github/workflows/release.yml and two new node scripts. First, before `changeset publish` the release job now polls npm until it lists the FFI and auth native packages that publish-ffi and publish-auth have just published. Second, a new eql-assets job decides from npm and the git tags, not from the run's own publish step, whether the EQL SQL, docs and image assets are still owed, and builds them at the commit that the `@cipherstash/eql@<version>` tag names. The four EQL jobs switch to `!cancelled()`. No library code, payload format or SQL changes. The main risk is that the repair path depends on two assumptions about changesets/action that could not be checked here: that it sets `publishedPackages`, and that it pushes the changesets tag, when `changeset publish` exits non-zero. If it does neither, the exact failure this change targets (EQL published and then the publish step fails) leaves eql-assets throwing on every push to main and the assets are still not built. That failure is loud and fails closed, so impact is medium. The unit and workflow-simulation tests are thorough, but they inject these assumptions rather than test them, and none were run.

behaviour_changes.description: publish-ffi and publish-auth now export a space-separated name@version `published` output. Before changesets/action, the release job runs scripts/wait-for-npm-versions.mjs, which polls `npm view <name> versions` every 15 s until npm lists every exported version. It gives up after 900 s, and the step has a 20-minute timeout. If the deadline passes, the release job fails before `changeset publish` runs. When neither publish job ran, the lists are empty and nothing is waited for.

The production EQL asset trigger moves from a step inside `release` (eql_published, computed from publishedPackages after a successful publish) to a new eql-assets job. That job runs whenever classify reports production mode and gate succeeds, whatever the result of `release`. It reports the assets as owed when the tree's EQL version is on npm (or in this run's publishedPackages) and no eql-<version> tag exists. It throws when no `@cipherstash/eql@<version>` tag names the publishing commit and this run did not publish the version.

eql-sql and eql-docs now build at the commit eql-assets names (the changesets tag commit, or GITHUB_SHA), not always at github.sha, and the GitHub release is created at that commit. A later push to main can therefore build and publish assets from an older commit's source.

The four EQL production jobs are now gated `!cancelled() && ...` with explicit result checks, not the implicit success(). They therefore run when `release` failed or was skipped, and when publish-ffi or publish-auth was skipped.

The GitHub expression evaluator moves from workflow-dispatch-job-conditions.test.mjs into scripts/__tests__/lib/expressions.mjs and gains a cancelled() model. No test case was removed from the existing file.

failure_scenarios.title: A failed `changeset publish` leaves neither publishedPackages nor the changesets tag, so eql-assets throws on every push instead of repairing
failure_scenarios.trigger: `changeset publish` publishes @cipherstash/eql@V and then exits non-zero (as in the 3.0.6 run). Or EQL 3.0.6, the tree version at head, has no `@cipherstash/eql@3.0.6` tag in the repository.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: eqlAssets() builds only when `thisRun` (the version is in the run's publishedPackages) or a `@cipherstash/eql@V` tag gives the commit. Otherwise it throws (scripts/eql-release-assets.mjs:91-106). Both sources come from changesets/action, and to my understanding of its implementation (not verifiable offline) it sets the publishedPackages output and pushes tags only after the publish command exits 0. The release job's comment and the tests assert the opposite (release.yml:504-509, eql-release-assets.test.mjs:88-111, 444-459), but they inject that behaviour rather than observe it. eql-assets' own `if` runs it on every production push where gate succeeds (release.yml:669-675), so with npm listing V and no tag of either kind the job errors on each push to main until someone pushes the tag by hand or bumps EQL.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The change does not fix the failure it targets. The EQL SQL release, docs bundle and image for V are still missing, and every release run on main shows a failed eql-assets job, which can hide other release failures. Nothing wrong is published: the script fails closed and tells the operator to push the tag.

failure_scenarios.title: The npm listing wait times out or does not match what changesets reads, which blocks or still fails the JS release
failure_scenarios.trigger: npm takes longer than 900 s to list a native package. Or `npm view <name> versions` answers from a cache node that already lists the version while changesets' own `npm info` lookup does not.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The wait step runs before changesets/action (release.yml:613-618). On timeout it throws and fails the job (wait-for-npm-versions.mjs:82), so `changeset publish` and the Version Packages PR update do not run for that push. Its success means one registry lookup listed the version; it does not guarantee the next lookup, made by changesets, sees the same.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The JS release, including an EQL bump, is held until someone re-runs the job. Or the E402 failure this change was meant to stop happens again. Both are loud and nothing is published wrongly, since the duplicate publish is refused by npm.

failure_scenarios.title: Repair builds publish SQL and docs built from an older commit with today's toolchain under an already-released version
failure_scenarios.trigger: eql-assets owes the assets for a version published by an earlier run, for example 3.0.6 on the first push after merge, and builds them at the changesets tag commit.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: eql-sql checks out the older ref and runs `mise run --force build --version V` (_build-eql-sql.yml:67,87) using the head revision's reusable workflow. AGENTS.md records that the EQL Rust toolchain is `latest` and that nothing proves regeneration reproduces npm's published bytes (AGENTS.md:487). Before this change the assets were built in the same run as the publish, which narrowed that gap but did not close it.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The GitHub release SQL bundle and the postgres-eql image for V could differ from the SQL inside the npm tarball for V, with nothing reporting it. Or the build fails because the old source does not match the current reusable workflow, which is loud.

evidence.claim: The release job exports published_packages directly from steps.changesets.outputs.publishedPackages. Its comment claims the action sets this even when `changeset publish` fails.

eqlAssets returns not-needed when the eql-<version> tag exists. It owes the assets when the version is in this run's publishedPackages or on npm, takes ref from the changesets tag (falling back to headSha only for this run's publish), and otherwise throws.
eql-assets runs on `!cancelled()` with production mode and gate success, whatever the result of release, and feeds PUBLISHED_PACKAGES to the script.
eql-sql, eql-docs and eql-image are gated on eql-assets.outputs.needed and build at eql-assets.outputs.ref. eql-image dispatches with update_floating_tags=true.
The wait step runs before changesets/action with FFI_PUBLISHED and AUTH_PUBLISHED taken from the publish jobs' outputs.
Polls every 15 s for up to 900 s, retries lookup errors, and throws on the deadline, naming the missing versions.
publish-ffi lists every tarball's name@version, including ones it skipped as already published, and writes them to the `published` output.
npmVersions runs `npm view <name> versions --json`, returns null on E404 and throws otherwise.
The decision tests inject publishedPackages and tag lookups. The repair case assumes a `@cipherstash/eql@3.0.6` tag exists, and the failed-publish case assumes publishedPackages is populated.
A job-graph simulation covers release failure, skipped native jobs, cancellation and the gate failing, plus wiring assertions for the eql-assets outputs and the ref inputs.
Unit tests of parseSpecs and waitForVersions cover the timeout, 404, error-retry and exact-version cases.

The release job uses changesets/action@v1.9.0. changesets/action runs the publish command with getExecOutput, which throws on a non-zero exit before the action pushes tags or sets the published and publishedPackages outputs. This comes from recollection of the action's source; v1.9.0 could not be checked offline.
The tree's EQL version at head is 3.0.6, the version the commit message says is on npm with no eql tag.
vitest is not installed in the checkout (No such file or directory), so the tests could not be run.
release.yml had 58 commits from 8 authors before base, 31 of them in the last 90 days. It is a frequently reworked file.
Runs are serialised per ref (concurrency group with no cancel-in-progress), so two pushes cannot both build eql-<version> at the same time.
The reusable SQL build checks out inputs.ref, runs `mise run --force build --version`, and creates the release at target_commitish.
release is skipped when an in-scope native publish did not succeed. eql-assets no longer depends on its success.
The diff removes no it()/describe() cases. It moves the evaluator to lib/expressions.mjs and adds a cancelled() test.
AGENTS.md records that the EQL Rust toolchain is pinned to latest and that nothing proves regenerating from source reproduces npm's published bytes.
